cover.sticker: One line in your proposal fixes it

blocks.text: Most studios send the invoice when the project ends. It feels fair: you did the work, so now you bill for it.
Here's what that habit costs you.
A four-week project. An invoice at the end, on net 30. A client who pays a little late, like most clients do.
That's about 60 days from the first day of work to the money.
For those 60 days you pay your team, your rent and your software. The client pays nothing yet.
You're lending them the whole project for free.
The fix is the three-payment split:
A third when the work starts.
Write the split into the price section of your proposal, before anyone signs. Send the first invoice with the signed proposal.
Then it isn't a surprise. It's how you work.
Priya runs a video studio. She used to wait about 60 days on every project.
"New projects pay the first third within a week of kickoff."
